summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with productive cough, high fever, confusion, and leukocytosis. Imaging revealed lung opacities suggestive of pneumonia or aspiration, and a urine culture confirmed E. coli UTI, likely complicated by a malpositioned Foley catheter. His delirium was attributed to the infection and recent cocaine use. He was treated with IV antibiotics, transitioned to oral Augmentin, and improved clinically. His chronic kidney disease remained stable, and he was discharged home with follow-up plans for urology, infectious disease, and primary care. Blood cultures were negative at discharge but required outpatient follow-up.
